heading: EXT. STAGECOACH STOP BUILT AROUND A DRY WELL - DUSK

units.text: EXT. STAGECOACH STOP BUILT AROUND A DRY WELL - DUSK
A whitewashed adobe station squatting on a plain the color of old bone.
At its center, ringed by a low stone wall, a dry well yawns black and deep.
A cottonwood, long dead, throws a bony shadow across the porch.
Wind pushes a tumbleweed in slow circles around the well.
SILAS MCALLISTER, fifties, the station keeper, stands on the porch in a faded blue shirt, a rag hanging from his belt, a shotgun leaning against the post.
His face has been burned by thirty summers into something like leather.
He watches the road.
WIDOW HARGROVE, sixties, steps down from the idle stagecoach in black crepe and a veil she lifts to look at the sky, her mouth set tight.
She carries a carpetbag that clinks.
REVEREND TOBIAS CRANE, forties, follows her, thin as a rake, Bible clutched to his chest.
His collar is yellow with dust.
JACK "BLACKBIRD" TALLCHIEF, thirties, the stage driver, a lean Cherokee man in a flat-brimmed hat, climbs down last and stretches his back, one hand on the wheel hub.
He says nothing.
His eyes go to the well.
A YOUNG WOMAN, twenty, in a gray traveling dress, remains seated in the coach.
She does not move.
Her eyes are fixed on the porch.
Her hands are in her lap, bound by a length of leather cord.
DEPUTY LIAM FINNEGAN, thirties, rides up on a sweating bay, dismounts, loops the reins, and walks stiffly to the coach door, one hand on his holster.
He is the woman's escort.
He has not slept in two days.
Water's gone, folks. I'll not lie to you.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: How gone?
units.name: WIDOW HARGROVE

units.text: Gone since June. Well's dry as a Methodist's Sunday.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: Lord deliver us from jests.
units.name: REVEREND CRANE

units.text: Station keeper, I need a room with a lock on the door.
units.name: FINNEGAN

units.text: Got one. Back of the kitchen. No window.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: That'll do.
units.name: FINNEGAN

units.text: She hasn't said a word since Dry Fork.
units.name: BLACKBIRD

units.text: She won't.
units.name: FINNEGAN

units.text: Blackbird crosses to the well and looks over the stone lip.
He kneels and picks up a pebble and drops it.
Nobody breathes.
A long second later, from deep down, comes a small, dry click.
Forty feet. Maybe fifty.
units.name: BLACKBIRD

units.text: Mr. McAllister, I paid for a bed and a bath.
units.name: WIDOW HARGROVE

units.text: Ma'am, you'll get the bed.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: And the bath?
units.name: WIDOW HARGROVE

units.text: You can have the whole well, if you can find the water.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: The Young Woman turns her head, very slowly, and looks at the well.
Finnegan sees this.
He steps in front of the coach door to block her view.
Everybody inside. We stay the night, we leave at first light.
units.name: FINNEGAN

units.text: Deputy, is she a danger to us?
units.name: REVEREND CRANE

units.text: She's a danger to herself.
units.name: FINNEGAN

units.text: The devil has many faces.
units.name: REVEREND CRANE

units.text: This one's twenty and scared, Reverend.
units.name: FINNEGAN

units.text: The Young Woman looks at him now.
For the first time, she speaks, in a voice dry as paper.
Sir.
units.name: YOUNG WOMAN

units.text: Finnegan freezes.
My name is Eleanor Voss. I would like you to say it. Just once. Before we go in.
units.name: YOUNG WOMAN

units.text: Miss Voss.
units.name: FINNEGAN

units.text: Thank you.
units.name: ELEANOR

units.text: She steps down from the coach on her own, hands still tied, and walks toward the porch.
She passes the well.
She does not look at it.
She passes Blackbird, who takes off his hat.
She passes the Widow, who draws her veil.
She passes Reverend Crane, who clutches his Bible tighter.
At the porch she stops in front of Silas.
The room with no window.
units.name: ELEANOR

units.text: This way, miss.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: Silas opens the door.
Eleanor goes in.
Finnegan follows, and shuts it.
That wind's gone quiet.
units.name: BLACKBIRD

units.text: So it has.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: The tumbleweed stops circling.
The cottonwood shadow lengthens across the porch.
From deep in the well, softly, comes the sound of water, running.
Do you hear that?
units.name: WIDOW HARGROVE

units.text: Dear God. It was never dry.
units.name: REVEREND CRANE

units.text: Silas lifts the shotgun.
Blackbird crouches at the stone wall.
The water rises, rises, a silver glimmer in the black, and the sound grows into a hollow, hungry roar.
